topics.topic: read_spooled_file contract for digest/size/media_type: required validation vs ignored/metadata-only
questions: If provided digest/size/media_type do not match the located SpooledFile record, must the call be refused, or are those fields ignored for lookup and not validated?
Are digest/size/media_type in read_spooled_file request required-and-validated against the record, optional metadata, or ignored entirely for correctness?

quotes:
`read_spooled_file` takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue — and names
it by its identity — `run_id`,
`producer_node_id`, `map_index` (omitted for a node that is not mapped),
`attempt_number`, `producer_port`, `list_index` (omitted for a `one`
port) — the lookup identity; its digest, size and media type only describe it
judgement.why: The text explicitly says lookup is by the identity fields, while digest/size/media_type are descriptive only.

topics.topic: store.read_records behavior for invalid argument shapes/elements (including whether internal_error is part of the contract)
questions: Is `internal_error` an official possible result of store.read_records for malformed relation arguments, and must callers handle it as part of the operation contract?
What exact error/result is required if a caller makes an identity-mode call with zero identities, or mixes identity and relation arguments?
If `effects` is passed a malformed element tuple (e.g., node not in run version, wrong map_index presence), what must `store.read_records` return in that trusted path?

quotes:
A read by identity takes one or more identities and answers in the order
given, a repeated identity once.

A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and
answers `internal_error` — so does one that omits an argument its relation
names or passes one of another kind; that defect is decided before any record
is looked up.

The record a relation
names — every one of them — must exist, or the call is
`unknown_reference`, naming the first missing record in the order the
relation's name mentions them (A16 rule 1: checks in the order listed); from an existing
record, an empty answer is a result, not a refusal.

`effects.reach_operation_element` and `effects.operation_element_conclusion`,
  both called only by `runs` for an element of a run it has read — which make
  none of them and have no such refusal.
judgement.why: The spec already defines malformed-call handling (`internal_error`), identity-call cardinality, missing-reference behavior, and that those two trusted effects operations do not perform element-shape checks themselves.

topics.topic: Deterministic refusal-reason precedence when multiple roll_back_slot checks fail
questions: If multiple rollback checks fail (e.g., implementation not in slot/current contract and also no admitted verdict over current corpus), which failing check must be named as the reason?

topics.topic: Error classification when read_spooled_file has structurally invalid map_index/list_index presence
questions: When map_index/list_index presence is structurally wrong (present/absent contrary to node mapping or port cardinality), is the error `invalid_request`, `refused`, or `unknown_reference`?

topics.topic: How surface maps canonicalization failures from canonical_bytes to MCP error codes
questions: When `surface` calls `canonical_values.canonical_bytes` and it fails, must the MCP response code be translated to `invalid_request`, or passed through as `refused`?

topics.topic: Input boundary for canonical_values.canonical_bytes: raw JSON text vs already-parsed value
questions: Does this operation receive raw JSON text (where duplicate object keys are observable) or an already-parsed value (where duplicates may already be collapsed)?

topics.topic: Required cleanup action for earlier same-attempt spooled files when spool_file exceeds ceiling
questions: When one spool_file call crosses a spool ceiling after earlier files of the same attempt were already spooled, which operation is required to remove those earlier same-attempt files?

topics.topic: Whether internal_error is a refusal-class result or a separate result class
questions: Is `internal_error` part of the refusal channel (with refusal ordering rules), or a separate non-refusal result class?

topics.topic: inspect/list semantics for filter references that do not resolve: unknown_reference vs empty results
questions: For inspect/list operations using reference-like filter values that name no record, should behavior be `unknown_reference` or empty page?
